parsed.explanation: Combined federal-subnational regime creates high trans-visitor risk: passport/visa marker rules can refuse, strand, and pursue fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; national and local facility bans expose restroom use to trespass arrest; documented custody abuse, birth-sex placement, and denial of care; official counterterrorism and victim-charging show state threat framing. Partial protections—existing X-passports, court challenges, legal aid, national hate-crime and employment rulings—reduce but do not offset traveler-facing restrictions. No credible execution or imprisonment highly likely, so above severe anchors; still well below 0.35.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport/visa markers reset to birth sex; new X markers blocked; mismatch can trigger refusal, stranding, additional evidence requests, and fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; foreign advisories and reported confiscations show traveler-facing friction.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; ACLU suit and court challenges may slow or contest restrictions; legal-aid FAQ guides document mismatch; permanent fraud finding is not automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening applies nationally, so protective subnational rules do not prevent federal entry, document-verification, or refusal exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections removed hormones, cut hair, forced therapy, and denied care; immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; trans people placed/searched in men's facilities despite female markers; hospital care denied locally.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Courts may review custody conditions, and some policies are contested, but no operating safe-placement or care remedy is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch at border or a restroom/care encounter can escalate into federal or local custody, where birth-sex placement and abuse follow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars government-funded single-sex facility access congruent with identity; many subnational bans cover government buildings, schools, and some private settings; four criminalize use; documented capitol restroom arrest and severe municipal ordinance.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Exemptions, varied non-ban units, and court challenges exist; not all private settings covered; some anti-discrimination laws apply in certain subnational/municipal spaces.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules and local enforcement combine: visitor can face private refusal plus public-building trespass exposure depending on location and employee request to leave.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned in many units and in the division; funding freeze, service shutdowns, proposed reimbursement bars, and hospital records subpoenas indicate hostile care environment; adult visitor-specific emergency care is not clearly documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented. National health-care rules do not protect visitor continuity; general anti-discrimination laws are not care-access guarantees.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking or emergency treatment can force document/marker review, custody placement, and disclosure to authorities, especially for minors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' ideology for priority identification/neutralization; reward guidance references 'radical gender ideology'; police charged restroom victims rather than attackers, reinforcing threat framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and employment-discrimination ruling provide some recourse; several orders are contested or enjoined; official text says powers are not for mere disagreement, but atmosphere remains hostile.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat framing amplifies border, facilities, and police encounters by treating trans advocacy, document mismatch, or presentation as a security risk.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face care bans, school investigations, criminal risk for staff supporting social transition, and sports/records restrictions; a parent/guardian may face denial of continuity or document scrutiny when travelling with a child.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Marriage and adoption recognition do not create a traveler-facing care or school-access shield for trans minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian document mismatch, enrollment, clinic use, or school activity can trigger disclosure and enforcement under national and subnational rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented mob beating over restroom use with victims charged, attackers not arrested; division records a high reported trans-women killing rate, though undercounted and misreported; current violence frequency cannot be separated reliably from background.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Some subnational/municipal anti-discrimination and national hate-crime enforcement exist; advocacy monitors deaths; rule-of-law remedies may operate in other contexts.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police charging victims and severe ordinances convert social hostility into institutional exposure for outed visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement varies by border post, facility, custody actor, and subnational unit; fraud, restroom trespass, care denial, and counterterrorism linkage remain uncertain; unresolved bills and pending pleas.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active lawsuits, legal-aid guidance, existing passport validity, hate-crime and employment law provide partial relief; several executive orders are blocked or enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court injunctions can reduce immediate exposure but do not create a traveler-facing safe regime while hostile policies remain operative.

anchor_checks.comparison: The jurisdiction is above 0.15-A because it lacks explicit criminalization of trans presentation, execution threat, and wholly illusory remedies; courts, legal aid, existing passport validity, and hate-crime recourse operate, though custody abuse and border refusal remain severe.

It sits below 0.35-B. That anchor involves identity checks and short release without credible imprisonment; here documented birth-sex custody, sexual abuse, facility arrest, and fraud-based lifetime inadmissibility make post-discovery consequences more severe.

It is far below 0.55-B. That anchor's main risk is secondary screening and administrative refusal with appeals; this regime adds criminal facility exposure, custody abuse, care hostility, and official counterterrorism language.

parsed.synthesis: Federal document and border rules interact with local facilities and custody: a passport mismatch or restroom encounter can become refusal, stranding, arrest, or birth-sex detention. Subnational anti-discrimination law and court challenges give partial relief, but national executive orders, facility bans, custody practices, and threat framing remain operative. Adult travellers and travelling families face high risk; minors add care-denial exposure. No credible execution or highly likely imprisonment places it above severe, but not high-safety.
